Lucid Design Group was established in 2004 by founders Vladi Shunturov, Michael Murray, Gavin Platt, and John Petersen. The company's foundation traces back to research projects at Oberlin College focused on building sensor and metering infrastructure. This academic exploration into real-time feedback technology, led by faculty and students, laid the intellectual groundwork for Lucid's commercial offerings. Shunturov, who studied computer science and environmental studies, was instrumental in developing the company's early products and later served as CEO. The firm initially concentrated on providing building analytics systems through its "Building Dashboard" software, which offered web-based feedback on electricity, gas, and water consumption.

The company's primary offering evolved into BuildingOS, a software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform designed as a centralized operating system for commercial buildings. This platform aggregates and analyzes data from a wide array of sources, including utility meters, building automation systems, lighting controls, and IoT sensors, to provide a holistic view of building performance. The business model is centered on subscriptions to this platform, empowering clients like building owners, operators, and facilities managers to make data-informed decisions. Key benefits for clients include identifying operational inefficiencies, reducing energy consumption and costs, managing capital decisions, and improving overall business performance derived from their properties. The BuildingOS platform is distinguished by its ability to integrate with over 180 different building data systems, eliminating vendor lock-in and providing a single console for portfolio-wide performance tracking.

A significant milestone in the company's history occurred in February 2018 when it was acquired by Acuity Brands, a major provider of lighting and building management solutions. The acquisition was a strategic move by Acuity to merge its hardware expertise in digital lighting and sensory networks with Lucid's advanced software capabilities. vinfast.c: The story of VinFast begins not with cars, but with instant noodles. Pham Nhat Vuong, Vietnam's first billionaire, built his initial fortune in post-Soviet Ukraine with an instant noodle business. After selling it, he returned to Vietnam and founded Vingroup, a conglomerate spanning real estate, technology, and retail. With a vision to create a Vietnamese car brand for the world, Vingroup established VinFast in 2017. Initially, the company moved at an unprecedented speed. It acquired a GM manufacturing plant in Hanoi and partnered with established automotive players like BMW and Pininfarina to accelerate development. This strategy allowed VinFast to launch its first gasoline-powered cars in 2019, an incredibly short time for a new carmaker. The company's playbook was clear: leverage the resources of its parent conglomerate to build a national automotive champion. A pivotal moment in the VinFast story was its strategic shift to focus exclusively on electric vehicles. The company phased out its internal combustion engine models to compete in the burgeoning global EV market, a bold move for such a young brand. This transition set the stage for its next major chapter: a global expansion. In August 2023, VinFast achieved a significant milestone by going public on the Nasdaq through a SPAC merger. The event initially valued the company at an astonishing $85 billion, far exceeding established automakers. This IPO provided a massive injection of visibility and capital, signaling VinFast's ambition to compete directly with global EV giants. Today, VinFast represents a case study in industrial ambition, a national brand attempting to carve out its place on the world stage.

More about Bollinger Motors

Made with AI

Bollinger Motors, an American electric vehicle manufacturer, was established in 2015 by Robert Bollinger in the Catskill Mountains of New York. The founder's journey into the automotive world was unconventional; after graduating with an Industrial Design degree from Carnegie Mellon, he worked in advertising and later helped build and sell an organic cosmetic company. The capital from that sale provided the financial backing for Bollinger to pursue his lifelong passion for cars, initially sparked by a desire for an environmentally friendly and rugged truck for his organic farm.

The company's initial focus was on consumer-oriented, rugged, all-electric SUVs and pickups. In 2017, the B1 SUV prototype was unveiled, featuring a distinct, angular design that garnered significant attention. Following the prototype's debut, the company relocated to the Detroit, Michigan area to leverage the region's deep automotive engineering talent pool. A major strategic pivot occurred in early 2022 when Bollinger Motors indefinitely postponed its consumer models, the B1 and B2, to concentrate on the commercial electric vehicle market. This decision was driven by the assessment that the commercial segment was more prepared for electrification. This strategic shift culminated in the company becoming a majority-owned subsidiary of Mullen Automotive (NASDAQ: MULN) in September 2022.

Bollinger Motors now focuses on developing and manufacturing all-electric commercial trucks, specifically in Classes 4 through 6. The company operates as an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), selling chassis cabs to commercial fleets and upfitters who then add specific bodies like contractor beds or delivery boxes. Production of its first vehicle, the Class 4 Bollinger B4 Chassis Cab, began in September 2024 at a facility in Livonia, Michigan, managed by manufacturing partner Roush Industries. The business model involves direct sales to fleet management companies and sales through a growing national dealer network that also provides service. Revenue is generated from vehicle sales, with significant financial incentives available to customers through federal and state programs, potentially exceeding $100,000 per vehicle.

The flagship product, the Bollinger B4, is a Class 4 all-electric chassis cab built on a proprietary 40-inch wide frame, which is wider than the industry standard and designed to securely house batteries and components between the rails for improved safety and driving dynamics. It is powered by an 800-volt system and features two LFP battery packs from supplier Our Next Energy (ONE), totaling 158 kWh. This provides a range of up to 185 miles. The B4 delivers 323 horsepower and has a payload capacity of 7,325 pounds. Charging can be done via AC Level 2 in nine hours or DC Fast Charge in about two hours. Following the B4, the company plans to launch the Bollinger B5, a Class 5 truck with increased payload capacity, expected in 2026.
